construction.proof:
Cross-base whole-prism inclusion transfer

Fix canonical source P=B_p x[-h/2,h/2] and target T=B_q x[-H/2,H/2], p != q. Derive one scalar alpha>0 and a single canonical offset b with T+b contained in alpha P. For each complete source owner c_i+R_i P, replace its dilated copy alpha c_i+R_i alpha P by the whole target alpha c_i+R_i b+R_i T. All source owners, actual frames and source labels remain; inherited source separators prove disjointness because the targets are subsets of the same simultaneously dilated physical packing. The inverse decoder is c_i=(new_c_i-R_i b)/alpha before final common recentering and restoration.

The initial registration is identity between the canonical xy and z axes. Its inclusion inequalities are n_f dot b + max_v(n_f dot v) <= alpha beta_f for EVERY actual canonical source facet and every target vertex. No independent owner turns or angles occur. The cheap four-variable LP derives a candidate alpha,b only; canonical exact inclusion and full native checks are mandatory before a result can be promoted. The complete target ensemble is enclosed using actual transformed target vertices, then one common translation and outward restoration.

The first screen uses authenticated/reviewed complete sources already in the common-axis inventory plus current public/private deltas. It compares all supported target heights 1,3/2,2,3 against the latest complete scalar envelope. Unlike previous same-base axial changes, this source operation changes the whole polygonal footprint and charges all inherited rotations and new host walls. Source authors and parent provenance are preserved.
